content:
Apple TV's current lineup is strong, led by hits like *Slow Horses*, *Ted Lasso*, *Dark Matter*, and the new Matthew McConaughey comedy *Brothers*. But there's even more on the way. Here's a look at everything new on Apple TV in October.

*The Last First: Winter K2*

  • Release date: 2 October
  • Format: Film
  • Genre: Documentary

*The Last First: Winter K2*, directed by Amir Bar-Lev, tells a complex, heart-stopping yet deeply moving story that examines the extreme mountaineering industry and its ever-evolving culture. The film focuses on a 2021 expedition in which Icelandic climber John Snorri Sigurjónsson and a team made up of Pakistani father-and-son Ali and Sajid Sadpara set out to become the first to summit K2 during the harshest winter conditions. Along the way, they encounter influencer climbers and their film crews, paying clients on commercial expeditions, and legendary Nepalese mountaineer Nims and his Sherpa team. *The Last First: Winter K2* takes viewers up the frozen peak of K2, through unpredictable weather, and reveals an unexpected, layered story — one woven with strategy and determination, class and hierarchy, money and power — all unfolding in a life-or-death environment.

*The Sisters Grimm* (Season 2)

  • Release date: 2 October
  • Format: Series
  • Genre: Kids & Family

Two orphaned sisters navigate a town full of fairy-tale and fantasy characters, confronting heroes and villains alike while investigating the mystery of their missing parents. *The Sisters Grimm* blends exploration, fantasy, and adventure, offering meaningful lessons for viewers of all ages.

*Small Prophets*

  • Release date: 7 October
  • Format: Series
  • Genre: Comedy

*Small Prophets* is a comedy about eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley). Since his beloved Clea vanished seven years ago, he's been living a quiet life — working at a hardware store, visiting his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and hoping for Clea's return. One day, Brian shares an ancient recipe involving rainwater, horse manure, and a touch of alchemy. Sceptical but hopeful, Michael sets about creating homunculi — magical sprites that can predict the future — in hopes they'll answer his most pressing question: "Will I ever see Clea again?"

*Matchbox The Movie*

  • Release date: 9 October
  • Format: Film
  • Genre: Action

*Matchbox The Movie*, adapted from the classic Mattel toy, is a pulse-pounding, globe-trotting adventure about a group of lifelong friends whose lives are turned upside down when CIA undercover agent Sean (John Cena) — their long-lost former leader — returns to their small town, and they're accidentally swept up in a heart-stopping, world-saving mission.

*Tenzing*

  • Release date: 16 October
  • Format: Film
  • Genre: Drama

*Tenzing*, based on a true story, tells the little-known tale of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok). A gifted Himalayan mountaineer, he joined New Zealand climber Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) as one of the first to summit Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo) and supported by expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe), the pair persuade Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) to let Tenzing join the British expedition as a team member rather than a porter. While Western climbers see "Everest" as a peak to conquer, Tenzing reveres "Chomolungma" as a sacred goddess of the mountains. What follows is an ascent marked by tensions of background, class, and ambition — and by the perils of the mountain itself. But far from the world below, empire, status, and ambition fade away, leaving only two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and, for Tenzing, the realisation of a lifelong dream and spiritual calling.

*Where's Wanda?* (Season 2)

  • Release date: 21 October
  • Format: Series
  • Genre: Dark Comedy

Apple's first German-language series, *Where's Wanda?*, is a dark comedy about Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, who are desperately searching for their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda, who disappeared without warning months earlier. After the police investigation hits a dead end, the family takes matters into their own hands, with the help of their tech-savvy younger son Ole, who acquires surveillance equipment. Posing as electricity company workers, they plant listening devices throughout the neighbourhood and half the surrounding suburbs — only to discover that their neighbours' true selves behind closed doors are nothing like they appear.

*Nocturne*

  • Release date: 30 October
  • Format: Series
  • Genre: Crime Drama

The series tells the story of Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber). A former military man turned homicide detective, he grew weary of years on the streets of Philadelphia and moved to a small town in western Pennsylvania in search of a quieter life. But when the town and his family come under attack from cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (Graham), Jonah must protect everything he holds dear. As the urgent hunt for Jurek's final victim forces Jonah to deploy his surrogate daughter, FBA agent Saga Bauer (Beetz), to confront Jurek head-on — how far will Jonah go?

New episodes: *Slow Horses*, *Brothers* and more

Apple TV will also roll out new episodes of several currently airing series in October, including:

  • *Ted Lasso*: Jason Sudeikis-starring comedy, new episodes airing through 7 October
  • *Last Seen*: crime thriller, new episodes airing through 7 October
  • *Slow Horses*: acclaimed British spy drama, new episodes airing through 21 October
  • *Dark Matter*: Joel Edgerton-starring sci-fi series, new episodes airing through 30 October
  • *Brothers*: comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, new episodes airing through 4 November

Which of these new October releases on Apple TV are you planning to watch? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV costs US$14.99 per month, and you can also enjoy a discounted bundle through Apple One.
